title: Adaptive stepwise traffic controller for canary rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a configurable policy engine that drives canary rollouts using adaptive, stepwise traffic schedules. This engine should support declarative traffic splits, time/metric-based step transitions, shadow traffic forwarding, A/B experiment variants, and automatic rollback when guardrails trigger. The goal is a reusable controller that product teams can reference in rollout configs (json/yaml) and that integrates with Console for observability and with the serving runtime for enforcement and graceful fallback.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Teams can declare a canary rollout with arbitrary step schedule (percentages and durations) and the controller enforces the traffic split.
2) The engine supports shadow traffic routing and an opt-in A/B experiment mode.
3) Guardrails (error rate, latency p95, regression delta) can be configured per rollout and trigger automatic rollback if breached.
4) Rollouts are observable in Console with per-step metrics and can be paused/resumed/cancelled.
5) Integration tests simulate traffic and show correct step progression and rollback behavior.
6) Safe defaults exist for short-lived rollouts and production rollouts; no user action should cause >3x customer error spikes.
implementation_plan:
- Design: finalize rollout config schema and guardrail operators (thresholds, windowing, statistical test). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Adaptive+Rollout+Design
- Controller: implement state machine that reads rollout config and issues traffic routing commands to routing service.
- Metrics: wire up existing tracer and metrics exporter to compute per-step aggregates (error-rate, p95, throughput).
- Auto-rollback: implement policy decision module with hysteresis to avoid flapping; add cooldowns.
- Console: add a minimal UI to create rollouts and view per-step metrics; link to rollout API.
- Tests: unit tests for policy logic, e2e tests using canary simulation harness, chaos tests that force metric anomalies.
- Rollout: feature flag + staged rollout to internal customers, then general availability.

2026-03-10: Risk: statistical significance checks can delay progression for low-traffic endpoints. Mitigation: support minimum sample sizes and allow manual override in Console (requires audit logging).
final_notes: Next steps: land rollout config parser and minimal controller loop (scheduling + metric evaluator) in a feature branch. Coordinate with Observability to ensure 1s metric granularity for p95 during canaries.
